transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?
What brings me in is, once I start eating comfort foods, I tell myself, “Maria, that’s enough,” but I just keep going back to the pot. It feels like I can’t make myself stop.
After one of these episodes where you feel unable to stop eating, do you ever try to get rid of the food or make up for it—like making yourself vomit, taking laxatives, or exercising a lot?
No, I don’t do anything like that afterward.
About how many days per week, on average, do you have one of these episodes where you feel unable to stop eating?
Most weeks, I’d say once or twice a week. It’s been that way since my friend passed, usually on those quiet afternoons after choir or gardening.
How long ago did your friend pass away, and did the overeating episodes start right around that time or did they begin earlier?
It was about three months ago when she died. The eating started after that, not before.
When you have these episodes of eating past the point of fullness, how do you feel afterward—do you feel distressed, guilty, or upset with yourself about the eating itself?
Yes. Afterward I feel ashamed and sad. Food used to mean family and caring to me, and now it feels like something I have to hide from the people at church.

Besides the eating episodes, since your friend passed, have you noticed changes in your mood, sleep, or interest in things you used to enjoy—like feeling persistently sad, low energy, or pulling away from activities?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed anything else in particular besides the eating.
Has this eating pattern or the way you're feeling affected your ability to keep up with your daily responsibilities or relationships—like at church, home, or with friends?
I still go to Mass and choir, and I take care of my home. But after one of those afternoons, I sometimes stay in and don’t call anyone. I feel too embarrassed.
During these episodes, would you say you're eating a noticeably larger amount of food than most people would eat in that same amount of time?

Yes. Some afternoons after choir or working in the garden, I’ll have a plate of rice and beans or chicken stew, then keep going back for more. By the end, I’ve eaten what feels like two or three meals.
During these episodes, do you often keep eating until you feel uncomfortably full physically, not just emotionally upset afterward?
Yes. By the time I stop, my stomach feels tight and heavy. I have to sit in my recliner and loosen my waistband because I’ve gone past what feels comfortable.
